messages.subject: unmarkedFitDS Backtransform Estimates
parts:
Hi all,

I've been trying to figure out how to interpret the estimates I obtain from my 'distsamp' model (unmarkedFitDS class). Unfortunately, the estimates are on the log-scale. I've seen some papers publish these estimates and standard errors as is, but I was wondering if there was a way backTransform the estimates into a more easily interpretable form. Performing a linearComb requires me to input covariate values and returns an overall density estimate, but I could also just use the predict function and it isn't getting at what I actually want. Specifically, I want to know how each covariate in my model is influencing my population density. 

I have tried using the predict function and running generalized linear regressions for each of my covariates independently as well as with my full model, but my data is not normal which requires further transformation and back-transformation. Is there a way to back-transform the estimates I obtained in my unmarkedFit instead of having to use the predict function or is it best to just interpret our results using the log-scale data? 

Thank you,

Rhett M. Rautsaw

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] unmarkedFitDS Backtransform Estimates
parts:
Dear Rhett,

you sure should use a predict function. After fitting the model, use it to predict the fitted model object for a new data set where you only vary one (or possibly two) covariate, but keep the other terms in the model constant (e.g., at 0 or at the covariate average). In this way you can then plot the predicted lambda against the variable covariate, while the effect of the other covariates is eliminated mathematically by keeping them constant.

There are lots of examples of how to form predictions in such models in the AHM1 book (and surely elsewhere too). Note also that function modavgPred in AICcmodavg can be tricked into producing point predictions with SEs and 95% CIs by providing a candidate list with a single model only (see page 265 in AHM1).

Best regards --- Marc
